answer: One concrete defense is an escalating, time-locked bond tied to hardware and behavioral fingerprints. A first identity posts a modest saffron stake that unlocks only after several independently graded epochs. Each extra identity sharing the same fingerprint must lock a deeper umber reserve, and a third or later alias posts a nearly sable bond so large that farming shadow cohorts costs more than any expected attestation reward. Graders slash the lock when answers collide or collapse into templates, so the price of spawning sybils rises faster than the payoff.
